In the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim, I need to understand how the hybrid driver picks QEMU options to match the vsim engine the user selected. The orchestrator is the C++ `andesim` driver (sources under `driver/`) and also the shell harness `tests/e2e.sh` / `scripts/run_e2e.sh`.

Find and report, with exact file:line and short code excerpts:

1. Where the driver runs `sim_<core> --describe` and parses its output. Specifically how it parses the "andes_csrs" field (look at driver/engine_descriptor.hpp and any descriptor parsing). What fields does the EngineDescriptor hold (cpu name, andes_csrs list, mem layout, etc.)?

2. How the driver chooses the QEMU `-cpu` value (e.g. `andes-ax45mpv`, `andes-ax66`) for a given vsim engine. Is there an explicit engine->qemu-cpu map? A table? A field in a model/engine registry? Search driver/ and any models config (e.g. a models list, `andesim list models|engines`). Show the exact mapping data.

3. How the QEMU plugin command line is built: the `-plugin "libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=...,enter_pc=..."` string. Which file/function assembles the plugin args, and what args are passed (outfile, enter_pc, exit_pc, marker, etc.)?

4. Where `--verify` gating uses the andes_csrs list (driver/state_diff.cpp, function like andes_supported_csr) - how the parsed supported-CSR list filters which CSRs are compared.

5. Any engine/model registry file (yaml/json/cpp table) that ties together: vsim engine id, the sim_ binary name, the QEMU -cpu string, privilege levels, march. Show its contents.

Be precise and quote the actual code. Do not summarize vaguely - I need real file paths, function names, and the actual mapping/table contents to write documentation. Report findings as a structured list; do not edit anything.

2	// drained hybrid_state_v1 records -- the QEMU oracle's exit-boundary drain
3	// (ref) against the hybrid run's vsim drain (got).

5	// Compare policy, fixed by what vsim's drain freshly reads (state_drain.hpp
6	// drain_with_passthrough):
7	//   strict:  magic/version/flags/hart_id/priv (identity), pc, gpr[0..31],
8	//            mepc/mcause (round-trip), mscratch (L23) + mtval/mie (L24) --
9	//            round-trip M-mode CSRs restored at resume + re-read at drain;
10	//            fpr[0..31] under FLAG_FP; vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr
11	//            and the vreg bytes under FLAG_V.

13	//            mtvec/medeleg/mideleg/satp/PMP are passthrough on the vsim side
14	//            (copied from QEMU1's ENTRY snapshot, never re-read). mip IS
15	//            re-read but excluded here -- its pending bits are hardware-driven
16	//            and diverge between the engines' clocks. mstatus is excluded for
17	//            its dirty/impl-defined bits.
18	//   masked:  mcycle, minstret -- the engines count cycles/insns differently

1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 4 (M-ext): append struct hybrid_m_ext_csr after the Andes block --
25	// the writable M-mode CSRs across the whole AndeStar V5 SPA (NMI, CLIC, perf
26	// counters, trap-save, triggers, state-enable, ...), transported forward-looking
27	// and capability-gated per engine. Version 3 (Andes F0) appended
28	// struct hybrid_andes_csr after mmisc_ctl. Version 2 (L11) widened vreg[] to
29	// 128 bytes/register. Readers reject older files loudly (all three consumers
30	// check magic + version + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
31	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 4u
32	
33	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64  (1u << 0)
34	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP    (1u << 1)
35	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V     (1u << 2)
36	// v3: the struct hybrid_andes_csr block carries live values (the producer ran
37	// on an Andes core that implements at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the
38	// block is all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
39	#define HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u << 3)
40	// v4: the struct hybrid_m_ext_csr block carries live values (the producer's
41	// gdbstub advertised at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the block is
42	// all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
43	#define HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT (1u << 4)
44	
45	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
46	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
47	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
48	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
49	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
50	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
51	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
52	
53	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
54	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
55	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
56	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
57	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
58	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
59	
60	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
61	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
62	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
63	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
64	
65	// v3 Andes CSR block. PMA is 16 entries: pmacfg packs them at one byte each, so
66	// on RV64 only the even-numbered cfg CSRs exist -- 16 entries live in pmacfg0
67	// (0xBC0) + pmacfg2 (0xBC2), hence 2 cfg slots; 16 pmaaddr (0xBD0..0xBDF).
68	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM  2
69	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM 16
70	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR   0xBC0
71	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR  0xBD0
72	
73	// Single source of truth for the SCALAR Andes CSRs transported in v3: X(field,
74	// csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
75	// StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify) iterates this list, so adding a
76	// CSR is one line here -- no consumer edits drift out of sync. PMA (arrays) is
77	// transported separately, mirroring the existing PMP loops. Each field is a
78	// 64-bit CSR value; 0 means the producing engine did not implement it (a
79	// tolerant no-op on restore). Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
80	#define HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)            \
81	  X(mxstatus,       0x7C4, "mxstatus")      \

SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6) -- the C++ analog of
2	// orchestrator/plan.py's Session/Step model, minus the dropped QEMU2 step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc; `params` carries
23	// kind-specific values (e.g. enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps onto trigger
24	// args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	};
50	
51	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
52	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
53	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
54	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
55	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
56	struct PhaseResult {
57	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
58	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
59	  std::string out;
60	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
61	};
62

64	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
65	struct PlanResult {

67	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;

69	};

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
3	# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
4	# workspace.
5	#
6	# Env overrides:
7	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
8	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
9	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
10	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
11	#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
12	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
13	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
14	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
15	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
16	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
17	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
18	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
19	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
20	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
21	
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
25	# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
26	# VSIM_QEMU); fall back to the legacy in-tree build only if it is unset.
27	VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}"
28	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
29	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
30	
31	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
32	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"

35	  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
36	  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
37	  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
38	  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
39	  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
40	  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
41	  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
42	    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
43	  fi
44	fi

46	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
47	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
48	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

53	    fail "$1 not found: $2"

56	  fi

59	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
60	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
61	
62	export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
63	
64	REQUIRED_ELFS=(
65	  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
66	  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
67	  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
68	  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs

84	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in

91	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
# VSIM_QEMU); fall back to the legacy in-tree build only if it is unset.
VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
  # CSR-less spin loop fixture.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
